notes: The title now asks Do better numbers mean better learning? On office return, the teacher notices disengagement, recalls the demand for measurable results and seeks a trackable sign. The longer second reflection holds four seconds before Level 1 asks Which sign would tell me the most?

Clicking the urgent email no longer changes the office camera. A separate unscaled reader fades in over 300ms, or 100ms with reduced motion. Text is laid out at its final size rather than magnified along with the office. The initial approach to the laptop is retained.

VISIT CLASSROOM is enabled and fully bright from its appearance. Reading and the optional thought do not lock the action. A separate footer keeps the action visible while body copy scrolls on small screens. Leaving cancels the reading hold; the departing reader is inert, ignores pointer events and is unmounted after pullback.

Both live and actual packaged opening suites verify the camera stays unchanged during mail opening, bright immediately usable actions, normal and early departure, desktop and touch sizes, reduced motion, all-three student gating, both revised office reflections and the Level 1 name handoff.

Normal student timing, sequential glowing arrow cues, classroom scripts and the existing Level 1 chapter introduction remain. Level rules, Gameplay and shared source are unchanged from the animation baseline.

All 26 checks passed without runtime errors. All six latest archives were built together and the actual complete-game and standalone entries pass the release suite. The five partner PNGs retain their original hashes.

Only animation/opening-integration is published. Stable game and preview branches retain their preceding commits. Offline Chromium checks use exact packaged HTML through an in-memory HTTPS route; they do not establish device-specific frame rates or subjective smoothness.
